regimen_profiles.clinical_summary: The aim is to control advanced bowel cancer and symptoms. The team reviews how well treatment is working and whether side effects remain acceptable; there is no single fixed number of cycles for everyone.
regimen_profiles.component_rationale: Cetuximab: Cetuximab attaches to EGFR on the outside of cells and blocks some growth messages. In this bowel-cancer plan, validated extended RAS testing helps identify whether treatment is suitable. Healthy skin also uses EGFR, so skin and nail effects need early care. Irinotecan: The body converts irinotecan into SN-38. This traps an enzyme called topoisomerase I while DNA is being copied, causing damage that can stop cancer cells dividing. Normal bowel and blood-forming cells can also be affected. Folinic acid: Folinic acid helps fluorouracil remain bound to an enzyme needed to make DNA. In this regimen it increases fluorouracil activity and can also increase its unwanted effects. It is not a vitamin supplement to start yourself. Fluorouracil: Fluorouracil interferes with the production and use of DNA and RNA, the instructions cells need to grow. The infusion extends exposure over approximately two days.
regimen_profiles.schedule_context: Cetuximab on Day 1 and Day 8. Day 1 FOLFIRI includes irinotecan, folinic acid and fluorouracil, followed by a 46-hour fluorouracil infusion with planned disconnection around Day 3. Repeat the reference cycle every 14 days while beneficial and tolerable.
key_points: Cetuximab on Day 1 and Day 8. Day 1 FOLFIRI includes irinotecan, folinic acid and fluorouracil, followed by a 46-hour fluorouracil infusion with planned disconnection around Day 3. Repeat the reference cycle every 14 days while beneficial and tolerable.

key_points: Cetuximab and modified FOLFOX6 start on Day 1, followed by one 46-hour fluorouracil infusion with planned disconnection around Day 3. Repeat every 14 days while beneficial and tolerable. No weekly Day 8 cetuximab is scheduled.
Metastatic colorectal cancer with validated extended RAS-wild-type status. The NCCP document retains older KRAS wording; the current Erbitux SmPC requires extended RAS testing.
Indirect for both schedule and backbone: OPUS used weekly cetuximab with FOLFOX4, not fortnightly cetuximab with modified FOLFOX6. Do not relabel OPUS results as an exact 00733 trial.
Clinical trial medians and response rates belong in the clinician evidence card; patient benefit explanations remain qualitative.

Fortnightly cetuximab infusion time is set from the dose and safe infusion rate; the first dose may take longer. Oxaliplatin and folinic acid are usually infused over about two hours, before fluorouracil. Blood review, preparation, premedicines and observation add time; infusion time is not the total appointment length. The fluorouracil pump runs for about 46 hours. Confirm where and when it will be disconnected, usually around Day 3; do not disconnect it yourself unless specifically trained. Cetuximab premedication includes an antihistamine and corticosteroid at least one hour before treatment. The first two infusions have a one-hour post-infusion observation; the team may change observation after two tolerated doses. The EMA product information specifies that chemotherapy starts at least one hour after cetuximab ends; the team includes this interval in your appointment.
Confirm the exact indication and regimen-specific prescription.

Discuss the treatment aim, alternatives, expected benefit, serious and lasting risks, fertility/pregnancy precautions and the contact plan. Confirm RAS selection for colorectal treatment, infusion premedication, skin care and post-treatment mineral checks. Explain DPD testing and the exact pump schedule.

Do not substitute the 00447 renal policy: this NCCP source permits specialist consideration of 50% oxaliplatin for CrCl below 30 mL/min or haemodialysis, whereas 00447 lists contraindication below 30 mL/min. The decision requires the source-specific renal and clinical review.

Prior grade 4 oxaliplatin neuropathy excludes the source rechallenge pathway even after recovery. Good recovery from grade 3 allows only specialist consideration, one level below the dose at onset, with previous dose history confirmed.
Folinic acid follows bolus 5-FU hold/omission. Bilirubin >85 µmol/L or absolute AST >180 contraindicates 5-FU; equality and uncertain AST unit/analyte require review.
CrCl <30 or haemodialysis permits consideration of 50% original oxaliplatin in this source; it is not an automatic prescription. Do not substitute a different FOLFOX regimen renal policy.

NCCP 00733 p9 retains an unlicensed-posology consent footnote. The current Erbitux SmPC section 4.2 now explicitly includes 500 mg/m² every two weeks for RAS-wild-type colorectal disease. Reconcile current local licensing/consent status; do not present the older footnote as an unquestioned current restriction or silently delete it.

administration.cycle_and_sequence: Cetuximab and modified FOLFOX6 start on Day 1, followed by one 46-hour fluorouracil infusion with planned disconnection around Day 3. Repeat every 14 days while beneficial and tolerable. No weekly Day 8 cetuximab is scheduled.
route_and_duration: Fortnightly cetuximab infusion time is set from the dose and safe infusion rate; the first dose may take longer. Oxaliplatin and folinic acid are usually infused over about two hours, before fluorouracil. Blood review, preparation, premedicines and observation add time; infusion time is not the total appointment length. The fluorouracil pump runs for about 46 hours. Confirm where and when it will be disconnected, usually around Day 3; do not disconnect it yourself unless specifically trained. Cetuximab premedication includes an antihistamine and corticosteroid at least one hour before treatment. The first two infusions have a one-hour post-infusion observation; the team may change observation after two tolerated doses. The EMA product information specifies that chemotherapy starts at least one hour after cetuximab ends; the team includes this interval in your appointment.
